title: Preview a batch selected from outcome discovery
description: Compose classify.outcome.list with the existing selected_outcomes apply.preview contract so an operator can preview a bounded batch without per-outcome CLI calls. Implements G7 and UC-CLASSIFY-007.
rationale: The correct bulk boundary is explicit outcome selection followed by the shipped frozen preview, not a new apply-all shortcut.
story_want: preview exact listed suggestions as one bounded batch
story_so_that: I can review frozen apply evidence before any Ledger mutation
acceptance_criteria: Given fresh suggestion outcome IDs returned by one evaluation, when the caller submits at most 200 unique IDs using apply.preview selection mode selected_outcomes, then the existing request schema accepts them unchanged and the preview returns frozen selection, category, rule-authority, evaluation, Ledger generation, category lifecycle, and expiry evidence.

Given unknown, duplicate-only, mixed-evaluation, non-suggestion, stale, archived-category, inactive-rule, or over-200 selection input, when apply.preview validates the batch, then it rejects or accounts for the full selection according to the released contract and persists no partial preview.

Given broadApplyAllowed is false, when a caller has a list page or active rule-set summary, then neither outcome.list, rule.list, rule-set.active.get, apply.preview, nor apply.run gains an implicit apply-all, unattended exact-rule, or unbounded mutation path.

Given preview succeeds, when Ledger or authority state changes before apply.run, then apply.run revalidates the frozen preconditions and fails or reports per-item outcomes under the released idempotent saga without applying stale authority.
Given preview is invoked, when Ledger allocation history is inspected before apply.run, then zero category assignments or corrections were created by discovery or preview.
security_criteria: Only exact caller-selected outcome IDs cross from discovery into preview; list filters, cursors, or report groups never confer mutation authority.
